# Agent Instructions

## Project shape

- This is a Node.js 18 TypeScript backend using Express, with route modules under `src/twitch/` and `src/youtube/`.
- Application startup and middleware registration are in `src/index.ts`; shared middleware, Redis setup, utilities, and type declarations live under `src/`.
- Treat `src/` as the source of truth. `backend_build/` is TypeScript output from `tsc` and should not be edited by hand.
- Because the project uses NodeNext ESM, preserve `.js` extensions in relative imports from TypeScript files.

## AI attribution

- Whenever creating a new file from scratch, add a top-of-file comment stating that the file was AI-generated by the model performing the work, naming that model.
- Whenever generative AI materially contributes to an existing file, add a brief top-of-file comment naming the model and describing in general terms what it generated or changed. The notice should indicate the approximate extent of the AI contribution without unnecessary detail.
- If the file format does not support comments, use its valid metadata mechanism when one exists; never make the file invalid just to add the notice.

## Commands

- `npm run tsc` compiles `src/` into `backend_build/`.
- `npm test` runs Jest tests.
- `npm run lint` runs ESLint across the repository.
- `npm run start:dev` starts the TypeScript server with `tsx watch`.
- `npm run start:prod` runs the compiled server from `backend_build/`.

Run the narrowest relevant check after a change, then run `npm run tsc` for TypeScript changes. Do not treat generated build output as a source edit.

## Code conventions

- Follow the existing ESLint style: double quotes, no semicolons, curly braces, and declaration-style functions where applicable.
- Keep TypeScript strictness intact (`strict`, `noImplicitReturns`, and `noFallthroughCasesInSwitch` are enabled).
- Prefer the existing parsing and error-handling utilities over duplicating validation logic.
- Keep route, middleware, service/API, and utility responsibilities in their existing directories.

## Local setup

- Required environment variables are checked in `src/envConfig.ts`; do not commit secrets.
- Redis must provide the RedisJSON module for the current Redis usage. See [`docs/misc.md`](docs/misc.md) for local Redis and Twitch application setup.
- See [`README.md`](README.md) for the project overview and deployed service link.
